dimensions.reasons: The author final image and usable Group A front/high views clearly show the requested industrial recycling line: a tall lime-green rear hopper frame with branded panels, a central processing unit, a separate left control cabinet, and a white/teal chevron conveyor. The overall studio-product presentation and green/white equipment identity closely follow the reference.
issues: The central crusher/compressor is substantially simplified relative to the reference, with far fewer mechanical housings, guards, fittings, and lower-machine detail.
The rear elevated structure reads more as a simple tall open bin than the reference's more complex framed processing/hopper assembly.
The prominent lower circular rotor/wheel-like machine component from the reference is not clearly reproduced.

dimensions.reasons: The main structures are visibly grounded and supported: the tall hopper frame has four feet, the processing unit has legs, the cabinet rests on the floor, and the conveyor has a braced rectangular underframe with visible casters. The conveyor's upper end reaches the machine-side feed area rather than floating in space.
issues: The white curved duct on the tall frame visibly terminates freely partway down the side in the final image and detail_controls view, without a convincing lower connection.
The conveyor-to-machine transfer is visually close but does not read as a fully enclosed, clearly joined transition hopper.
The dark component beneath the processing unit is an unclear angular mass rather than an identifiable, mechanically integrated lower assembly.

dimensions.reasons: The equipment silhouettes are independently readable as a hopper/frame, crusher unit, control cabinet, and inclined conveyor. Lime yellow-green primary paint, deep teal accents, white conveyor structure, GREENMAX/INTCO branding, teal belt, and repeated white chevron pattern are all visible in recycling_unit_final.png and the close views.
issues: The lime green is more fluorescent/neon than the softer yellow-green industrial paint in the reference.
Several machine surfaces remain broad, minimally articulated box forms, especially the lower processor housing.
The under-machine mechanism and some small control/inspection features do not have strong enough shape definition to read as functional components.

dimensions.reasons: recycling_unit_final.png is a clean, coherent studio render with soft shadows, a controlled neutral gradient backdrop, and a legible product-oriented camera angle. The equipment is presented consistently rather than as disconnected assets.
issues: The result has a simplified, toy-like CAD/model quality rather than the mechanically dense industrial realism of the reference.
Bright white frame members and pale interior surfaces are partially washed out, reducing edge contrast.
Material response is very uniform across much of the green machine, limiting the sense of painted steel panels, seams, and fabrication.

dimensions.reasons: The key spatial arrangement is correct in the final image: the free-standing control cabinet is on the left, the tall hopper assembly is behind, the processing machine is in front of it, and the conveyor projects down toward the right/front into the machine feed zone. Group A wide_front and wide_high also make the intended material flow layout understandable.
issues: The control cabinet is set farther away and appears more isolated from the processing unit than in the reference.
The connection between the conveyor's elevated discharge end and the processor inlet is less explicit than the requested added transition hopper.
The rear tower reads as more detached from the main unit than the integrated structure in the reference.

dimensions.reasons: The equipment shares a plausible common scale: the conveyor is long enough to serve the processor, the cabinet is human-height relative to the machine, and the tall rear frame is the dominant vertical element.
issues: The rear hopper tower is visually narrow and disproportionately tall compared with the compact processor beneath it.
The main processing unit looks smaller and less substantial than the reference machine relative to the tall structure and conveyor.
The conveyor is comparatively narrow and lightly built for the scale of the feed tray.

dimensions.reasons: The submitted final has soft studio illumination, a pale gray gradient environment, visible floor contact shadows, distinct teal belt coloring, and a gray metal-like control cabinet. The painted green frame and white conveyor are materially separated at a basic level.
issues: The requested brushed stainless-steel quality of the control cabinet is only weakly apparent; it largely reads as a smooth gray/white box.
The green steel structure appears smooth and plasticky rather than convincingly matte painted metal.
High exposure on white conveyor rails and interior panels suppresses material and edge detail.

dimensions.reasons: All principal requested categories are present and recognizable: control cabinet with colored controls, elevated branded hopper/frame, curved white duct, processor with a cylindrical side motor, teal-lined feed tray, mesh-cage accessory, and a wheeled white-frame conveyor with green chevrons.
issues: A distinct, clearly enclosed transition hopper between conveyor discharge and the processor inlet is not convincingly visible.
The reference's large lower wheel/rotor-like mechanism and several associated mechanical details are absent or reduced to an unidentifiable dark form.
The curved duct lacks an evident finished lower connection.
The control cabinet has fewer and much coarser visible control details than the dense reference panel.

criteria.criterion: The reconstruction forms a complete equipment line with the specified regional organization and reference-like relative scale hierarchy.
The left operating station combines the required cabinet identity, visible controls, and modified brushed-stainless finish.
The rear hopper retains its elevated support, salient reference construction, upper branding, and attached curved guide pipe.
The central processing assembly combines a recognizable shredding-and-compaction body, readable processing-region cues, and a plausibly mounted cylindrical drive motor.
The right conveyor combines the specified frame, patterned belt, attached casters, and gentler modified incline.
The added transition hopper physically and legibly connects the conveyor discharge to the main-machine inlet.
The complete equipment line uses the required palette and a distinguishable matte painted-frame material system.
The native scene and final render implement deliberate three-point soft product lighting.
The designated final render combines the specified studio background and camera composition with unobstructed educational readability and a clean product-grade finish.
criteria.evidence: The designated final render, recycling_unit_final.png, presents the complete lime-green processing line, separate control cabinet, elevated hopper structure, and full white-framed chevron conveyor in a clean elevated three-quarter view. The teal receiving hopper visibly connects the conveyor discharge to the processing machine, while the black side-mounted motor and front inspection/control region remain exposed. All principal assemblies are within frame against a pale gray-to-white studio gradient with clean soft shadows and no clutter or severe render artifacts.

criteria.criterion: A genuine high-resolution completed author render is delivered as an openable image.
The delivered Blender project is openable, editable, and suitable for later annotation and alternate camera views.

notes: This is a recognizable and clean reconstruction of the requested recycling line, with the essential cabinet, hopper tower, processor, and conveyor all present. Its main limitations are simplified industrial mechanics, a weakly resolved conveyor-to-machine transition, an unconnected-looking duct, imperfect proportions, and washed-out/materially uniform rendering.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
